questions.n: CATIA was developed by Dassault Systèmes to design fighter jets, allowing for the precise modeling of complex, curved surfaces.

questions.q: Which feature of the 'Seagram Building' plaza was a revolutionary urban design move in New York City?
o: The use of heated sidewalks to melt snow
Setting the building back from the sidewalk
questions.n: Mies van der Rohe created a public open space, which led to the 1961 Zoning Resolution encouraging plazas in exchange for extra height.

questions.q: The 'Jewish Museum Berlin' uses 'voids' to symbolize what?
o: The technical limitations of the site's foundation
The absence of Jewish life in Germany post-Holocaust
Ventilation shafts for the underground levels
questions.n: The empty, unheated concrete voids represent the physical and cultural erasure of a population.

questions.q: The 'Nakagin Capsule Tower' capsules were designed to be replaced every 25 years. Why did this never happen?
o: A change in Tokyo's zoning laws
The company that built them went bankrupt
The residents refused to leave their homes
questions.n: The design made it difficult to remove a single capsule without disturbing the ones above and below, making replacement financially unviable.

questions.q: In the 'Kimbell Art Museum,' how does Louis Kahn bring natural light into the galleries without damaging the paintings?
questions.n: Wing-shaped reflectors bounce light onto the concrete vaults, bathing the space in soft, indirect 'silver' light.

questions.q: What is the primary characteristic of 'Parametricism,' as seen in Zaha Hadid's Heydar Aliyev Center?
o: The use of rigid, repeating rectangular modules
A return to classical Greek and Roman proportions
The total elimination of all structural supports
Fluidity and continuous geometry driven by algorithms
questions.n: Parametricism treats all architectural elements as variable and mutually dependent, resulting in seamless, flowing forms.

questions.q: The 'Salk Institute' plaza is intentionally left empty of trees and landscaping. Why?
o: Because the saltwater air would kill most plants
To prevent roots from damaging the underground labs
To emphasize the view of the horizon and the ocean
To provide a landing pad for medical helicopters
questions.n: Luis Barragán advised Kahn to leave it empty, calling it 'a facade to the sky' that creates a spiritual connection to the Pacific.

questions.q: Which material did Mies van der Rohe use for the columns of the 'Barcelona Pavilion' to achieve a weightless appearance?
questions.n: The cruciform steel columns are clad in shiny chrome to reflect the surroundings and 'disappear' into the space.

questions.q: What was the main criticism of the 'Portland Building' by Michael Graves shortly after its completion?
o: The roof leaked whenever it rained
It was dark and uncomfortable for the employees
It was built using low-quality recycled wood
The colors were too bright for a government building
questions.n: The small windows and heavy decoration made the interior feel cramped and dimly lit compared to modern glass offices.

questions.q: The 'Bruder Klaus Field Chapel' was constructed using a process called 'rammed concrete.' How was the interior shape created?
o: By inflating a giant balloon inside the wet concrete
By burning away a teepee of 112 tree trunks
By hand-carving the concrete after it dried
questions.n: The concrete was poured around the logs, which were then set on fire over three weeks to leave a charred, ribbed void.

questions.q: In the 'Villa Savoye,' what is the purpose of the 'Pilotis'?
o: To lift the building and allow the landscape to flow underneath
To serve as chimneys for the central heating
To provide a space for hanging laundry
To protect the house from forest fires
questions.n: This is the first of Le Corbusier's 'Five Points,' emphasizing that the ground should belong to nature or the car.

questions.q: The 'Institut du Monde Arabe' in Paris uses mechanical apertures on its facade. What determines when they open or close?
o: The number of visitors inside the building
A timer set to the Five Pillars of Islam
The amount of sunlight hitting the sensors
questions.n: The 240 photosensitive diaphragms act like camera lenses, closing to reduce glare and opening to let in light.

questions.q: Which phrase did Louis Kahn famously use to describe the relationship between light and architecture?
o: Architecture is the learned game of forms assembled in the light
The sun never knew how great it was until it hit the side of a building
Light is the only true building material
questions.n: Kahn believed architecture was the 'making of a room' and that natural light was essential to define space.

questions.q: The 'Centre Pompidou-Metz' by Shigeru Ban features a roof inspired by what object?
questions.n: The intricate hexagonal timber grid was modeled after the structural logic of a traditional bamboo hat.

questions.q: What is the 'Bilbao Effect'?
o: The economic revitalization of a city through iconic architecture
The rapid oxidation of titanium in salty air
The psychological disorientation caused by curved walls
The tendency for museum visitors to get lost in spiral ramps
questions.n: The success of Gehry's museum transformed Bilbao from a failing industrial port into a global tourism hub.

questions.q: In the 'Glass House,' where are the only opaque walls located?
o: There are no opaque walls; even the bathroom is glass
In a central brick cylinder containing the bathroom
Only in the bedroom at the back of the house
On the side facing the neighboring road
questions.n: Philip Johnson used a single brick core to hide the 'private' functions, leaving the rest of the house transparent.

questions.q: Which project by Norman Foster is often called the 'Gherkin' due to its distinctive shape?
questions.n: The building's aerodynamic, tapering form and diagrid skin give it its famous pickle-like nickname.

questions.q: The 'Fallingwater' house was famously built over a waterfall. How is the house anchored to the site?
o: It is not anchored; it rests purely by gravity
Steel beams anchored into the natural boulders
A deep foundation of concrete piles in the riverbed
Suspension cables from the surrounding trees
questions.n: Wright used the existing rock outcroppings to support the massive concrete cantilevers.

questions.q: Which architect designed the 'Museum of Islamic Art' in Doha at the age of 91?
questions.n: Pei traveled extensively across the Muslim world to study geometry and light before designing this masterpiece in his 90s.

questions.q: The 'TWA Flight Center' is an example of 'Neo-Futurism.' What was Eero Saarinen trying to convey with its shape?
o: The efficiency of a modern factory
The shape of a giant radar dish
The spirit and excitement of flight
The stability of an ancient temple
questions.n: The soaring concrete vaults look like outspread wings, capturing the optimism of the early jet age.

questions.q: What is the primary material of the 'Ningbo History Museum' facade?
o: Debris and tiles from destroyed local villages
Polished grey granite from a local quarry
questions.n: Wang Shu used 'wa pan' masonry, a traditional technique for building walls with salvaged materials, as a critique of rapid urbanization.

questions.q: The 'Unité d'Habitation' features a 'Roof Garden.' What was the social purpose of this level?
o: A private penthouse for the architect
A community space with a nursery, gym, and pool
A mechanical floor for boilers and air units
A secure landing area for airships
questions.n: Le Corbusier wanted the roof to be a shared public square for the residents, replacing the ground space taken by the building.

questions.q: In Mies van der Rohe’s 'Seagram Building,' the I-beams on the facade are not actually structural. What is their purpose?
o: To provide visual rhythm and emphasize height
To channel rainwater away from the glass
To serve as lightning rods for the skyscraper
To act as tracks for window-washing robots
questions.n: The real steel structure had to be encased in concrete for fireproofing; Mies added bronze I-beams to 'show' the structural logic aesthetically.

questions.q: Which landmark by Renzo Piano was nicknamed 'The Shard' by its critics?
questions.n: The name came from a critic who claimed it was a 'shard of glass through the heart of historic London,' but the name was later adopted officially.

questions.q: The 'Cardboard Cathedral' in New Zealand by Shigeru Ban was built following what event?
o: The host city's selection for the Olympics
A government initiative for sustainable housing
questions.n: Ban designed it as a temporary replacement for the Christchurch Cathedral which was destroyed in the 2011 earthquake.

questions.q: In the 'Seattle Central Library,' what is the 'Book Spiral'?
o: An automated robotic system for book retrieval
A decorative art installation made of old paper
A staircase that leads to the rare manuscripts room
A continuous ramp that organizes books by Dewey Decimal number
questions.n: It allows the library to expand its collection without moving sections to different floors, keeping them in a single sequence.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Le Corbusier's 'Five Points of New Architecture'?
questions.n: Le Corbusier championed the 'Free Facade' and 'Free Plan' which were only possible by eliminating load-bearing walls.

questions.q: The 'CCTV Headquarters' in Beijing is famous for its loop. How do the two towers connect?
o: They don't actually touch; it is an optical illusion
A series of thin pedestrian sky-bridges
A central third tower supports them both
questions.n: The two leaning towers are joined at the top by a L-shaped section that juts out into space, creating the loop.

questions.q: In 'Habitat 67,' what was Moshe Safdie's goal for urban living?
o: Making all units identical to promote equality
Giving every apartment a private garden and fresh air
Reducing the cost of construction by using plastic
Creating the tallest concrete building in Canada
questions.n: Safdie wanted to combine the density of an apartment building with the privacy and amenities of a suburban house.

questions.q: The 'Glass House' and the 'Farnsworth House' are often compared. Which one was completed first?
o: They were both completed in the same year
The Farnsworth House was never completed
questions.n: Philip Johnson finished his house in 1949, two years before Mies completed the Farnsworth House in 1951.

questions.q: What is the material of the 'white' walls in Richard Meier's buildings, like the Smith House?
questions.n: Meier is known for his 'Whiteness,' using bright panels to reflect light and contrast with the natural green landscape.

questions.q: In the 'Sendai Mediatheque,' the 'tubes' serve three functions. Which of these is NOT one of them?
o: They function as light wells to bring sun into the core
They act as water storage for fire emergencies
They provide the main vertical structural support
questions.n: The tubes house vertical circulation (elevators), utilities (pipes), and structural support, but not bulk water storage.

questions.q: The 'National Assembly Building' of Bangladesh is surrounded by an artificial lake. Why?
o: To prevent the heavy building from sinking into the soft soil
To provide a moat for military defense
To serve as a cooling reservoir for the air conditioning
To represent the importance of water in Bengali culture
questions.n: Kahn integrated the building with water to reflect the geography of the delta and provide a sense of monumental isolation.

questions.q: Which architect is known for the 'Pritzker-winning' design of the Therme Vals?
questions.n: Zumthor is the master of phenomenology, focusing on the sensory qualities of materials like stone and water.

questions.q: The 'Vitra Fire Station' by Zaha Hadid is rarely used as a fire station today. What is it used for now?
o: It was demolished to make room for a new building
An exhibition space for the Vitra Design Museum
A private residence for the CEO of Vitra
A storage facility for luxury cars
questions.n: The fire station's sharp angles were eventually deemed impractical for daily fire-fighting operations.

questions.q: In the 'Barcelona Chair,' what is the material of the frame?
questions.n: The X-shaped frame is made of stainless steel (originally chrome-plated) to match the columns of the Barcelona Pavilion.

questions.q: The 'Louvre Pyramid' was designed by I.M. Pei. Why did he choose a pyramid shape?
o: It is the most stable geometric form that minimizes visual bulk
Because it was the cheapest shape to build with glass
To reference Napoleon's campaigns in Egypt
To house the museum's collection of Egyptian mummies
questions.n: A pyramid provides a large entrance area with minimal impact on the views of the surrounding historic palace.
